transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Stocks opened higher this morning as investors wait for news this week on inflation and interest
rates.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones industrial average rose about 220 points in
early trading.
The Commerce Department will issue its report card on inflation later this week, a measure
that's closely watched by the Federal Reserve — prices have been climbing faster than
the central bank would like.
But Fed policymakers are expected to hold their benchmark interest rates steady when
they meet on Wednesday.
Oil prices have inched down from recent highs.
Triple A says the average price of gasoline has fallen by about a penny a gallon in the
last week, while the average price of diesel fuel has increased about three cents.
Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start this year.
The market research firm Nielsen IQ says sales through mid-October were down nearly 7 percent
from a year ago.
Candy makers remain hopeful, however, that shoppers will opt for more treats by Saturday.
Scott Horsley in NPR News, Washington.
Iran is bracing for a return to war after the U.S. midterm elections next week.
The U.S. and Israel have said this round of strikes may be "fiercer than the last two."
And Piers Hadil Al-Shalchi reports.
Iran is striking a defiant tone, as the U.S. and Israel say they're preparing to resume
strikes after the midterm elections.
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Bakhai said that Iran has "never left the
negotiating table," but is also prepared for war.
President Trump has claimed that Iran's military infrastructure was destroyed, but Iran has
come back forcefully in the past.
Iran expert Trita Parsi of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft says Trump underestimates
Iran.
"Even if its arsenal has been depleted, its capacity to rebuild and produce missiles and
other forms of munitions is very, very formidable."
He says Tehran wants to make the cost of a new conflict so high that Washington has to
back down.
Hadil Al-Shalchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
Libya's government has summoned America's top diplomat in that country.
Libyan officials are protesting weekend remarks President Trump made in a campaign rally against
Libya.
NPR's Jewel Bright reports.
Libya's Foreign Affairs Ministry summoned the Shah Jaffez of the U.S. Embassy on Sunday
to protest remarks made by President Trump.
The president was campaigning over the weekend for Georgia's Republican Senate candidate
Mike Collins and said this of his Democratic challenger.
Libya's government says Trump's comments were offensive.
Trump later posted on Truth Social where he praised Libya and reaffirmed his administration's
commitment to work with the North African country.
Jewel Bright, NPR News, Vegas.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Artificial intelligence company Anthropic has released paperwork to prepare for its initial
public offering.
The company's main AI agent is Claude.
Anthropic hopes to start selling shares on Wall Street as soon as possible.
The company also hopes to raise billions of dollars, although the total amount that Anthropic
is seeking is not yet known.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says this has been the worst year for measles
in the United States in more than three decades.
And Pierre Chandelis Duster reports Pennsylvania has been especially hard hit.
Pennsylvania officials are urging residents to get fully vaccinated against measles amid
new cases across the state.
The Pennsylvania Department of Health says over 1,300 cases of measles have been confirmed
in 44 counties across the state so far this year.
There were at least 21 new measles cases as of last week.
More than 250 people have been hospitalized and 5 people have died from measles in Pennsylvania.
Across the US, there have been more than 4,500 measles cases so far, which is more than double
the number of cases last year.
The CDC says that the vaccination status of 96% of those who have contracted measles this
year is "unvaccinated or unknown."
Chandelis Duster, NPR News.
Tonight is Game 3 of the World Series.
The Tampa Bay Rays will host the Milwaukee Brewers.
Milwaukee leads two games to none in the best of seven series.
Neither team has ever won Major League Baseball's championship.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Stocks open higher as investors await this week's inflation report and Fed decision
Oil prices dip slightly while diesel fuel prices rise, according to AAA
Halloween candy sales through mid-October are down nearly 7 percent from last year
Iran defiantly says it is prepared for war as U.S. and Israel plan renewed strikes after midterms
Libya summons top U.S. diplomat over Trump's remarks about Libya at Georgia rally
Anthropic files paperwork to prepare for initial public offering on Wall Street
CDC says 2025 is the worst U.S. measles year in over three decades; Pennsylvania hard hit
Tampa Bay Rays host Milwaukee Brewers in World Series Game 3 tonight
